sources.finding: Lanes Desktop MCP is a research preview enabled under Settings > Integrations > Lanes MCP, with one-click connection for supported agents. sources.title: Lanes primary client and public repository scope
sources.locator: Install; What it is; Part of Lanes; public tree
sources.finding: The official repository presents Lanes Desktop as a native macOS application. Its complete installation/client description names no browser or native phone client. The public tree contains plugin documentation, not the proprietary desktop execution core. Separate Link, Forms and Compute products are not Desktop clients.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Working with Sessions
sources.locator: What is a session; Many sessions per issue; Session Settings; Starting a session; Know what a session is doing; Resuming; History; Stopping; Sending to Review
sources.finding: Each session is a local PTY running Claude Code or Codex (any other CLI runs as a plain shell) attached to an issue; an issue can host several named sibling sessions sharing its worktree. Plan or Implement start modes; Gateway and Flags chosen per session. Statuses busy, awaiting input, stopped, exited, error; detection rewritten in v0.40/v0.41. Claude restarts pass --resume; lanes_resume_session re-attaches. JSONL History per session. Cmd+R moves to Review keeping sessions alive; the Meta tab shows tokens, cost and runtime.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Collaboration
sources.locator: Local or remote; Inviting members; Coordinate; Claiming issues and locks; Taking over an issue
sources.finding: Remote workspaces sync to the Lanes server; Admin and Editor roles; workspace-scoped chat (not per issue). Starting a session assigns the issue and locks it while active; other members cannot start a session until it stops. Taking over a stopped issue shows whose session it was; AI takeover clears the previous terminal history and starts fresh, bare terminals reconnect. Deleting a workspace is permanent.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Lanes Desktop MCP
sources.locator: Enabling; Connecting an agent; What the server exposes; Connect a client by hand; Research preview
sources.finding: Research-preview MCP server built into the app on localhost:5353 (SSE), toggled in Settings, Integrations; one-click connect writes a lanes-desktop entry into Claude Code or Codex config. Tools list, search, create, update, move and delete issues (filter by column, label, component or free text), start Claude Code, Codex or shell sessions (plan mode, prompt, flags, env, worktree), stop sessions, read history, stats and terminal; with GitHub or Linear connected, read, search, create and comment on their issues. Tool approvals are the client's mcp__lanes-desktop__* permissions.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Building Loops
sources.locator: Before you start; Loops you can paste and run; A loop you can run as-is; Stop a loop running away
sources.finding: Loops are driven by an external agent over the Desktop MCP and need Lanes running to serve it. Recipes include /loop cadence prompts, a fix-until-green loop that repeats at most 3 times, and a JSON-RPC script with a 15-minute wall-clock timeout; guidance asks for a wall-clock timeout and a max-iteration cap. Lanes has no PR tool; sessions open PRs with their own shell.

sources.title: Lanes docs: The Issue Board
sources.locator: What each column means; Make the columns match how you work; Creating issues; Editing issues; Act on several issues; Narrow the board
sources.finding: Statuses grouped Not started, In progress and Done are configurable; issues hold title, description, instructions (sent as the initial prompt), CLI and worktree strategy; edits autosave. Done column can be cleared from its menu. Bulk Stop, Remove and Complete. Per-project and per-worktree tabs; sort options.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Gateway
sources.locator: Creating a profile; Point a CLI other than Claude Code; When a change takes effect; troubleshooting 401 and 400
sources.finding: Provider profiles route a session to Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter or z.ai, chosen per session; credentials are applied as process environment, never on the command line or in ps. Claude Code variables are mapped; other CLIs use a free-form env table, but Codex's file-based config cannot be routed. Changes apply at the next session start. Documents 401 and adaptive-thinking 400 failures and fixes.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Worktree Management
sources.locator: Choose how an issue gets its working directory; Running dev servers and tests; Finishing work; Auto-cleanup
sources.finding: Strategies Default (Create for git repos), None (run in the project directory), Create and Select. Worktrees isolate agents from each other; env vars and config files in a worktree are local to it; port-derivation guidance. Test Worktree then Complete & Merge (commit, merge into base, complete issue); clean worktrees auto-removed, dirty ones warned.

sources.title: Lanes docs: Settings & Configuration
sources.locator: Workflows (Issue automation); CLI flags; Notifications
sources.finding: Issue automation: PR opening moves an issue to Review, a draft PR parks it in Misc, sessions follow Planning/Implementation, and Done stops sessions (each toggle on by default). Per-repo CLI flags and env prefix variables are typed into the terminal, land in scrollback and ps, and must not hold credentials; flags such as --dangerously-skip-permissions can be set. Notifications cover the Done sound.

sources.title: Lanes docs: GitHub Integration
sources.locator: Connecting GitHub; Importing an issue; Refreshing; From the agent; What the GitHub grant does not cover
sources.finding: GitHub OAuth brokered by the Lanes API with repo and read:user scopes; token stored locally in integrations.json. Import copies title and body with a link marker; refresh overwrites from upstream. MCP tools list, search, read, create issues and comment on issues or PRs. PR creation happens through gh inside a session.

sources.finding: Linear OAuth brokered by the Lanes API with read scope that also allows creating issues and comments; tokens stored locally, refresh through the Lanes API. Agents always see every team. Projects, cycles and priority are not mapped; core fields are title, description, state and URL; state mapping is manual.

sources.title: Lanes Security & Trust
sources.locator: Overview; Controls (Identity & Access); Data; Sub-processors
sources.finding: Local-first: prompts and terminal output stay local; Desktop MCP runs locally. Remote workspace data in Supabase EU with row-level security; members see only issues and sessions they can access; synced data is issue metadata, membership, issue comments and session pointers. SSO via Google implemented; SAML and enterprise SSO and admin audit logs Planned. Sub-processors: Firebase Authentication, Supabase, Resend, Stripe, Google Analytics 4 (consent-gated) and Sentry. Retention account-bound, deletion within 30 days.

Remote workspaces, Slack and Automations are marked Coming soon; Lanes Compute GPUs are Coming soon and billed separately.
